misconfig_patterns: No auth code path exists in the dominant community pattern (hand-rolled FastAPI/Flask wrapper) — the wrapper repos this class is cloned from ship zero auth by default
--host 0.0.0.0 binding is the standard tutorial/README recipe (Docker CMD/uvicorn examples), not an operator opt-in decision
No rate limiting on /predict or /detect — GPU inference compute theft via unbounded upload-and-infer loop
Uploaded images persisted to disk (input/ or uploads/ dir in most tutorial templates) and served back statically — past-inference image disclosure
Model file path and weights filename often echoed in /docs, error tracebacks, or startup banner — discloses which .pt/.onnx checkpoint (possibly proprietary/fine-tuned) is loaded
FastAPI default /docs and /openapi.json left enabled in production — full route + schema disclosure with zero effort

MMDeploy-Triton deployments inherit Triton's own unauth-by-default posture (no auth flag in default docker run) — /v2/models lists all loaded model repos, /v2/models/<name>/config exposes full model config

active_probe.false_positive_check: CONJUNCTIVE MATCH REQUIRED, not single-marker: generic "FastAPI" title alone matches thousands of unrelated APIs. Must confirm (a) a /predict or /detect path key in openapi.json AND (b) at least one CV-specific response-schema field name (boxes, confidences, class_ids, detect_objects, xyxy, class_id) in the same document. Even then this is a hand-rolled-pattern match, not a branded-product match — HIGH residual false-positive rate because /predict + FastAPI is also the default template for non-CV ML serving (tabular models, NLP classifiers, recommender endpoints). No single string in this class is as reliable as ComfyUI's http.title:"ComfyUI".

deployment_tells: No canonical single-product signature exists — this class is a convergence of independent tutorial/template repos (Alex-Lekov/yolov8-fastapi, dankernel/YOLOv8-FastAPI, WelkinU/yolov5-fastapi-demo and dozens of forks/clones), not one codebase

Ultralytics itself ships no official self-hosted HTTP server — 'yolo predict' is CLI/library only; Ultralytics' own hosted inference is a cloud SaaS endpoint (Ultralytics Platform), out of scope for self-hosted unauth discovery

MMDetection/OpenMMLab ships no native REST server either — MMDeploy is an SDK/C++ inference library; HTTP exposure only happens when an operator bolts on Triton or TorchServe (via .mar archive) themselves, inheriting THAT platform's fingerprint rather than an MMDetection-specific one
Docker Compose is the dominant packaging pattern for the FastAPI/Flask wrapper class — docker-compose.yaml with uvicorn CMD and 0.0.0.0 bind is copy-pasted near-verbatim across forks

Response JSON field-name convergence across forks (boxes/xyxy/confidence/class_id/class_ids/detect_objects) traces back to Ultralytics' own Results object attribute names (.boxes.xyxy, .boxes.conf, .boxes.cls) — a genuine cross-repo fingerprintable signal even though the wrapper code differs
pivot_paths: GET /docs or /openapi.json → full route map + request/response schema (recon without a single detect call)
POST /predict or /detect → arbitrary image upload for unbounded GPU inference (compute theft)
GET /v2/models (Triton-backed MMDeploy) → loaded model repository names, versions, backend (TensorRT/ONNX/TorchScript)
GET /v2/models/<name>/config (Triton-backed) → full model config including input/output tensor shapes, dynamic batching settings
Static file serving of uploads/ or results/ dir (common in tutorial templates) → prior-submitter image disclosure
Startup banner / traceback path disclosure → local filesystem path to the .pt/.onnx checkpoint, sometimes revealing project/client name in the path string
vulnerabilities: No-auth-by-design in the dominant hand-rolled FastAPI/Flask wrapper pattern — there is no upstream CVE because no vendor ships auth for this pattern to begin with

GHSA-9pf3-7rrr-x5jh (InternLM/lmdeploy) — arbitrary code execution via insecure deserialization in torch.load(); relevant to the broader PyTorch-checkpoint-loading class this platform inherits, not MMDetection/MMDeploy itself

December 2024 Ultralytics PyPI supply-chain compromise (versions 8.3.41/8.3.42 trojanized with XMRig cryptominer via GitHub Actions branch-name injection) — supply-chain risk to the ultralytics package itself, not a runtime auth/RCE flaw in deployed inference servers; noted for operator patch-hygiene context only
